core_obligations: Dispose of the unit case and set up the blowup: if a or b is a unit the statement is trivial with R = R', so assume a, b in m; set I = (a, b) and work geometrically with X = Proj(oplus_{d >= 0} I^d) over Spec(R) (proof lines 576-580).

Show the blowup is finite and affine over R: it is an isomorphism over the punctured spectrum U, projective, and its generic points all lie in U; hence by the finite-in-codimension-one criterion the morphism X -> Spec(R) is finite, so X = Spec(R') with R -> R' finite, and since R_a = R'_a a power of a (and thus of m) annihilates R'/R (proof lines 581-595).

Produce the common factor: IR' is locally principal by the blowing-up lemma, and R' is semi-local, so IR' = (t) for some t; writing a = a't and b = b't gives nonzerodivisors a', b' and the equality R' = a'R' + b'R' (proof lines 596-601).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a, b in the maximal ideal and pass to the blowup of R in I = (a, b) (proof lines 576-580).
Use the blowing-up facts plus the finite-in-codimension-one criterion to see that the blowup is finite and affine: X = Spec(R') with R'/R killed by a power of m (proof lines 581-595).
Use that IR' is locally principal over a semi-local ring to write it as (t), giving the common factor t and the equality R' = a'R' + b'R' (proof lines 596-601).
difficulty_reason: The lemma turns a pair of nonzerodivisors in a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring into a pair with a common factor after a finite ring extension killed by a power of the maximal ideal (statement lines 567-572). The proof replaces the plausible algebraic argument by a geometric one: it blows up R in I = (a, b), shows the blowup is finite over Spec(R) by combining projectivity, the fact that all generic points lie over the punctured spectrum, and the finite-in-codimension-one criterion, and then uses that a locally principal ideal over the resulting semi-local ring is principal, which produces t with a = a't, b = b't (proof lines 578-601). The non-routine content is precisely this combination: finiteness of the blowup is what makes R' a ring of the required shape, and semi-locality is what upgrades locally principal to principal. The claim is H2.
